title: Raspberry Pi and Single-Board Computers
welcome_lead: A £30 Linux computer for the classroom — and the satellite.
meta_desc: A-Level D&T: Raspberry Pi single-board computer and embedded Linux.
final_note: From hobby kit to global infrastructure.

concepts.def: Single-board Linux computer, first released 2012, UK Foundation.
General Purpose Input/Output — pins for digital I/O.
Hardware Attached on Top — Pi-specific expansion board.
System on Chip — integrated CPU, GPU, RAM controller.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Raspberry Pi, designed in Cambridge UK and launched in February 2012, aimed to revive entry-level computer science teaching. Over 60 million units have been sold globally.
Pi runs full Linux with display, networking and storage — heavier than Arduino but capable of vision, web servers, complex logic. Pi 5 (2023) has a quad-core 64-bit ARM Cortex-A76 at 2.4 GHz.
The 40-pin GPIO header carries digital I/O, I2C, SPI and UART. HATs snap on top to add sensors, displays, motor drivers — standardised by the Raspberry Pi Foundation in 2014.
